title: Heart-rate rise per achieved MET did not establish incremental cross-hospital coronary-disease prediction
abstract: A primary-literature-motivated endpoint representation, (peak heart rate − resting heart rate)/(achieved MET − 1), was tested in archived public angiographic referral cohorts. The underlying physiology is established, not a new biomarker. In 291 Hungarian development records, adding the ratio to a model already containing both heart rates, MET, duration and standard clinical/exercise measures slightly worsened five-fold out-of-fold log loss (0.382084 to 0.383352). Applied without target fitting to 146 eligible Long Beach VA patients, AUC changed from 0.713816 to 0.717654 (difference +0.003838; paired patient-bootstrap 95% interval −0.003845 to +0.012610). Log loss decreased by 0.005386, with an interval spanning no gain. Joint source/target refit uncertainty was wider. Medication/protocol adjustment reversed the AUC direction. Thus incremental transportable benefit was not established. This is not an equivalence test or a refutation of chronotropic physiology.
